theorem: No eta*-integral irreducible rational cubic exists in the Lucas plane; hence no complete curve of geometric genus 0 on X has a cubic Lucas image (M12-C closed), and Conjecture A2.C holds through degree 3: a nonconstant k(t)-MSS3 in characteristic 0 has plane image of degree >= 4.
method: A rational curve with cubic image is a birational degree-3 map (p:q:r): P^1 -> P^2, eta*-integral (A8.11), through >= 3 triple points (A8.15) moved to t = 0, 1, infinity, with branch tangents there among the integral lines through the points (Lemma T, entry 151). Point and tangency conditions are linear in the 12 coefficients and lambda_1, lambda_inf; the integrality identity E(t) = T(p, q, r; dp, dq, dr) = 0 (T the coordinate-free form of eta* times the nine lines) gives the ideal I in the family parameters. Verdict per sub-case: the family is empty (inconsistent linear system), or every point of V(I) is a map of rank <= 2 onto a line (each 3x3 minor of the coefficient matrix lies in the radical of I, or I = 0 with all minors identically zero). The 4,280 sub-cases (3-subsets of the eight triple points x admissible tangents) reduce to 597 D4-orbit representatives since T is D4-invariant.

four_parameter_cross_check.note: the earlier implicit method (cubics through the three points with prescribed tangents, four homogeneous parameters, four random projective charts): partial modular run; every isolated solution a product of integral lines, every positive-dimensional component proven non-reduced over its function field (the divisibility test is vacuous on a squared line); superseded by the parametrized method
